merge.title: Pre-PIN "device words": two BIP-39 words from SAES-CMAC(DHUK) over the PIN prefix, shown mid-entry so a substituted unit is noticed before the last four digits are typed
merge.threat:
Whole-device substitution of a unit the user has already verified and set up (evil-maid, lookalike swap). A trojan with different silicon harvests the 8-digit PIN on its own screen while the attacker holds the genuine unit. Nothing today proves "this is my unit" before the PIN is committed: the 8-word boot fingerprint is image-derived and identical on every unit (secure/src/measured_boot.rs:161-170), it is currently dark on a cold-booted sealed pq1 (#705), and enter_pin() only advances `pos` with no mid-entry device check (secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:54-146).

Not in scope, and the proposal must say so: (a) an implant or malicious firmware on the user's own die, where the words are correct; (b) interception before first setup, where the user simply learns the fake's words.
merge.proposal:
One firmware feature. No SE change, no board change, no new flash state.

1. Derivation. At the pos 3 -> 4 long-right transition in `enter_pin` (secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs, the `pos += 1` arm), compute `tag = cmac_dhuk(DOMAIN || prefix_len || prefix_ascii)` with the existing secure/src/hw/saes_cmac.rs:44. Map the top 22 bits to two BIP-39 words using the wordlist helpers already linked (`sphincs_tz_bip39::word_bytes_at`). Zeroize the tag.
   - DOMAIN is a new fixed-length label, e.g. `pq1-pin-words-v1`. It must not be a prefix of, or collide with, the existing DHUK-axis labels `se050-scp03-{enc,mac,dek}-v1`, `se050-admin-pin-v1`, `optiga-pbs-v1` and the salted `-v2` PBS label (secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs:457-491). The implementer should confirm the DHUK KDF's message framing so a truncated words tag can never equal a derived-key block input.
   - The prefix never leaves the MCU. No I2C traffic, and no interaction with page 124, E120 or the SE050 UserID.

2. Render. One interstitial screen ("Your device words: W1 W2", long-right continues, long-left goes back), on both the legacy 16x4 path and the ui-px path.
   - Under ui-px it must use the secret/forced-frame route (`px::screens::show_with(.., &[secret])` -> `push_secret_word`, secure/src/ui/px/screens.rs:108, pqsigner-ui-px/src/rows.rs:197), not plain `show()`.
   - On the legacy path use `secret_glyph_cols` (secure/src/ui/secret_text.rs:73-82).
   - #784 is a live bug of exactly this class (secret text on a non-forced frame), so the render needs a test that the frame is forced.

3. Call sites. The hook is inherited by every consumer of `enter_pin`: boot unlock (secure/src/main.rs:4163), the PendSV idle re-unlock (main.rs:4553), CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK, and `enter_pin_with_confirm` (pin_entry.rs:236).
   - Set-PIN in the wizard is where the user first sees and records the words, plus one explicit "write these down, they belong to this device, not to your seed" page.
   - The `e2e-test` arm of `enter_pin` (pin_entry.rs:173) compiles the hook out.

4. Query throttle. MCU-side and stateless: an S-SRAM per-boot cap (e.g. 3 word-derivations per power cycle, after which the interstitial is skipped with a loud "words unavailable, reboot" page, never silently). No flash counter, because CLAUDE.md forbids new per-signature flash state and there is no battery. The enumeration floor is therefore the per-boot cap times roughly 7 s boot plus four 500 ms long presses (secure/src/hw/buttons.rs:183) through the two-button UI. It is not an SE timer.

5. Always on, not an opt-in toggle. A toggle needs a persistent bit, which re-imports #601's "no free page" blocker (geometry/src/lib.rs:103-118). Always-on is fully stateless.
   - The words must render identically whether or not a wallet exists, and for every prefix. They are a function of (die, prefix) only, so they leak neither wallet existence nor which PIN (real or duress) is being typed.
   - The words survive a wipe. Document this as intended.

6. Fence. The words are meaningful only when DHUK is per-die, i.e. after the RDP-2 self-lock. At RDP-0 DHUK is an ST constant and every bench board shows the same pair. Gate the user-facing claim on `rdp2-self-lock`, and label the screen "BENCH - not device-unique" otherwise. In the shipping flow the wizard already runs after Phase A's RDP-2 burn.

7. Docs. Amend docs/security/user-device-verification.md with the scope statement and residuals, and cross-link #601. Do not create a new doc.

Optional v2 (owner decision; not part of the baseline): replace the fixed 4-digit hook with a user-triggered, hidden-length prefix of 2-6 digits, as Coldcard does, to enlarge the enumeration table.
merge.rationale:
All three members propose the same feature. Their shared SE-keyed mechanism does not survive contact with the drivers:
- The SE050 driver has no in-SE MAC command (grep for hmac/MACOneShot/CryptoObject over secure/src/se050 is empty).
- The OPTIGA driver has HMAC verify only (DecryptSym 0x20, secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs:160-167, 902-946), with no EncryptSym generate.
- A new OPTIGA secret OID with its own LUC is an irreversible metadata ceremony inside deferred S-1 territory.
- Neither SE has a clock, so "rate-limited in silicon to ~2 s" is unrealisable. The only SE levers are lifetime counters, which either burn budget or brick usability.

SAES-CMAC(DHUK) gives the same guarantee, since in both routes only secure firmware on the genuine MCU can invoke the MAC. It has no SE surface, and it binds to the MCU die. A board that keeps the user's SEs but swaps the MCU shows different words, which the SE route would not catch until the transport-key rotation (#268) lands.

Lead fact (d), that any secure image can select DHUK, does not weaken this threat model. Malicious code on the genuine die yields correct words under either route, so it is a residual, not a refutation.

Because the words are derived, the feature sidesteps #601's storage blocker entirely. Incremental flash is about 1-3 KB (wordlist and CMAC are already linked). That is small, but it lands in an image that is already 76,949 B over the slot with ui-px.

members.note: Passed all three round-1 lenses with corrections. Kept: prefix-derived two-word check at PIN entry, the 22-bit / two BIP-39 word mapping, separation from the PIN attempt counters, the wizard learn step, the #601 pairing. Changed: the SE050/OPTIGA CMAC object is replaced by cmac_dhuk; the in-SE 2 s rate limit is replaced by an MCU per-boot cap; 'off by default' becomes always-on (a toggle needs storage); the threat is narrowed to whole-device substitution (its 'genuine unit with implant and cloned shell' case gets zero protection); the vendor precedent is corrected (Coldcard's rate limit is bootloader/compute cost, not SE policy; Foundation shipped Security Words in Passport Core before Prime; the 35c3 source is irrelevant).

Passed all three round-1 lenses with corrections. Kept: the hook after the first 4 digits, CT/forced-frame render, invariant #2 untouched (the PIN compare stays in the SEs; the words are a separate keyed function). Changed: SE HMAC/CMAC route dropped in favour of DHUK-CMAC, as its own feasibility verifier recommended; 'rate-limited by SE policy' dropped. Its risk text ('the oracle yields nothing without the words') is corrected: filmed words plus later possession recover 4 of 8 digits, and filmed words alone let a clone replay them. Its dependencies on D-01/D-04 (CT/forced path, constant-weight pair) are not imported; only the existing secret-frame path is required.

No round-1 verdict; verified here.
Confirmed: no mid-entry hook (secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:122-137 only does `pos += 1`); the fingerprint is image-derived (secure/src/measured_boot.rs:161-170); #601 is OPEN and blocked on geometry; #700 is OPEN; Trezor has no equivalent (grep over trezor-firmware @6ab39e95cf returns zero hits for anti-phish / security word / pin prefix).
Refuted or dropped: 'OPTIGA PRESSEC object gated by its own LUC' and 'SE050 object under a dedicated UserID' (no MAC-generate in either driver; LUC is a lifetime count, not a rate; the OPTIGA object is an S-1-class ceremony); 'rate-limited by that SE counter'; 'prefix hashed before leaving the MCU' (moot, it never leaves); 'object in the wipe sweep so no words exist after wipe' (inverted: DHUK words survive a wipe by design and must be wallet-independent); 'decoy has its own key' (one DHUK; words depend only on the prefix, which is the deniable outcome with no owner decision needed).
Kept: 'no new flash page', which is true only for an always-on design.
kind corrected from mixed to firmware (no board change).

dropped_parts: SE050-resident CMAC/HMAC key object (IMP-10, D-09, pin-08): the driver has no in-SE MAC command, and creating the object lands in the production-quarantined first-boot object-layout flow. No security gain over DHUK-CMAC.

OPTIGA DeriveKey / PRESSEC object with a dedicated LUC (IMP-10, pin-08): needs the unimplemented EncryptSym 0x94 HMAC-generate plus an irreversible metadata ceremony in deferred S-1 territory (recorded decision: OPTIGA ship-blockers are deferred by design). A LUC is a lifetime usage cap, not a rate limit.

'Rate limit enforced in SE silicon, ~2 s per query' (all three): neither SE has a time base, and SE050 POLICY_OBJ_* has no throttle bit. It also has no vendor precedent: Coldcard's delay is bootloader/bus compute cost.

Off-by-default toggle (IMP-10, D-09): needs a persistent bit, and geometry has no free page (the #601 blocker). Replaced by always-on stateless behaviour. If the owner insists on a toggle, it must live in an already-owned field and becomes a separate decision.

Claim that the words defeat 'a genuine unit with an implant and cloned shell' or 'an implanted one with its own firmware' (IMP-10, D-09 threat text): refuted by both feasibility verifiers and by docs/security/user-device-verification.md:25-30 (a fake image on the same die has the same DHUK).
'Words must not exist after wipe / under duress' (pin-08): replaced by the stronger property that the words are independent of wallet state and exist for every prefix.

Separate decoy key for the duress PIN (pin-08): unnecessary. `duress-pin` is an optional feature that is not in any Makefile ship recipe (secure/Cargo.toml:425; no Makefile hit), and prefix-only derivation already gives plausible words for any PIN.
D-09's hard dependency on D-01/D-04 (forced CT path, constant-weight word pair): not part of this cluster. Only the existing secret-frame render is required.
IMP-10's 35c3 'Modchips of the State' source: a server BMC implant talk with no hardware-wallet content.
Fixed 2 s hold on every unlock: dropped as a security mechanism, since the per-boot cap carries the load. It also avoids the per-unlock UX tax.
tracked_issues: #601 (open): the same lookalike-swap threat via a stored user-personalised boot artifact, design-first and blocked on storage geometry. Its body names docs/security/user-device-verification.md as the amend target. It does not cover derived prefix words.
#700 (open): trusted-UI flows, including button PIN entry and the PendSV re-unlock, have never been exercised on pq1 silicon. Prerequisite for validating this feature.
#705 (open): the FSBL fingerprint is dark on a cold-booted sealed pq1. Explains why no pre-PIN user-visible check works on the production unit today; not the same mechanism.
#784 (open): restore-wizard letters render on a non-forced frame, bypassing the CT blitter and the F-24 force path. Same render class the words screen must not repeat.
#268 (open): first-boot provisioning and RDP-0 shipping blocker. Per-die DHUK finality (the RDP-2 self-lock) is what makes the words device-unique.
#249 (open): triple-UID supply-chain attestation. Adjacent (firmware- or companion-verified binding), not a user-visible pre-PIN check.
#206 (open): SE050 boot-time variant assertion. Adjacent (chip substitution), not device substitution.
decision_conflicts: docs/security/user-device-verification.md:25-30 (design record): fake firmware on the same die has the 'same DHUK once it self-locks', and nothing computed inside the device distinguishes it. This limits the scope rather than blocking: the words cannot be sold as firmware-authenticity or transit-interception protection, only as post-setup whole-device substitution detection. The RDP-0 SWD check stays the sole pre-setup defence (invariant #10).

CLAUDE.md 'No new per-signature flash state' and geometry (every page owned, the #601 blocker): the design must stay stateless, so the query cap is per-boot SRAM and there is no stored toggle or stored words.
OPTIGA S-1/S-2/S-3 deferred by design (memory feedback_optiga_shipblockers_deferred): rules out any variant that needs a new OPTIGA object or metadata.

Invariant #2 (PIN compare in SE silicon only): not violated. The words are a keyed function of a prefix, not a PIN comparison, and consume no attempt counter. They do add a second partial-PIN-dependent computation in the MCU, which should be reviewed as such.

Bench reality (memory project_pq1_bench_has_no_lcd, #700): the pq1 bench board has no panel and bench boards sit at RDP-0 where DHUK is constant, so neither the render nor device-uniqueness can be evidenced on today's bench.

ui-px flash budget (CLAUDE.md: 76,949 B over the secure slot): the roughly 1-3 KB increment is small, but it lands on an image that already does not fit. No new decision is needed, but it counts against the open flash lever.
prerequisites: The RDP-2 self-lock (rdp2-self-lock candidate, #268) must run before the wizard, so that DHUK is per-die when the user learns the words. This already holds in the candidate first-boot ordering, but that flow is production-quarantined.
A pq1 unit with a panel, on a non-e2e-test image (#700), to validate the interstitial, the button flow and the PendSV re-unlock path.
An RDP-1 or higher board to show that two dies give different words. At RDP-0 all boards match.
A domain-separation review of the new CMAC label against the existing DHUK-axis labels in secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs:457-491.
The #784 fix, or at least a regression test that the words frame is forced and secret, so the new screen does not inherit that leak class.
Owner decisions: always-on versus toggle, fixed 4-digit versus hidden-length prefix, and the per-boot cap value.
merge.precedent:
- Coldcard: anti-phishing words since the 2018 Mk1 public commit (`pin_prefix_words`). SE1 HMAC over a hashed 2-6 digit prefix under a key the MCU never holds, 22 bits shown as two BIP-39 words. Throttling is bootloader delay or chained-HMAC compute cost, not an SE policy.
- Foundation Passport: "Security Words" after the first 4 PIN digits, disabled by default, in Passport Core and inherited by Prime. The mechanism is unverified from code.
- Trezor: none. Grep of /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware @6ab39e95cf returns zero hits. Its only analogues are an unkeyed lockscreen label (core/src/apps/homescreen/__init__.py:89-92) and host-driven attestation (core/src/apps/management/authenticate_device.py:9).
- Ledger: none (cosmetic lock-screen image; companion-side Genuine Check).

The pq1 variant differs from Coldcard in keying on the MCU hardware-unique key instead of an SE secret. The security argument is the same, with no plaintext result on an SE bus.
merge.residual_after:
An attacker can still:
1. Live relay. The trojan forwards the 4-digit prefix, the attacker keys it into the genuine unit and returns the words. This is undetectable and is the same residual Coldcard accepts.
2. Pre-enumerate. With the genuine unit in hand, walk all 10^4 prefixes through the two-button UI. The floor is the per-boot cap times roughly 7 s boot plus long presses, i.e. hours to a day or so with a button robot, then load the table into the clone.
3. Replay filmed words. One camera or shoulder observation of the static pair lets a clone display it after any four digits, with no genuine unit needed. The same observation plus later possession recovers 4 of 8 PIN digits by enumeration, leaving 10^4 candidates against a 10-attempt budget.
4. Run malicious code on the user's own die (RDP-2 or TrustZone break, signed malicious update, implant on the genuine board). The words are correct.
5. Intercept before first setup. The user learns the fake's words; only the RDP-0 SWD verification helps.
6. Tap the display bus passively. The words and digits are still broadcast (the F-24 residual).
7. Capture the 4-digit prefix on the trojan before the user can abort.
8. Rely on the user. The words are advisory: a user who ignores or forgets the pair, or blames a wrong pair on a typo, gets no protection. A mistyped prefix also produces a false alarm.
9. Exploit resale. The words survive a wipe, so a previous holder of the die knows its table.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: a derived, stateless (die, prefix) -> two-word check at PIN entry is feasible with code already linked, needs no SE or board change, is untracked, and does narrow post-setup whole-device substitution. I confirmed that enter_pin has no mid-entry hook (secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:54-146), that cmac_dhuk exists (secure/src/hw/saes_cmac.rs:44), and that PROD_SHIP_FEATURES includes saes-dhuk and rdp2-self-lock (Makefile:2718). All seven tracked issues are open with the stated titles.

It is not refuted, but four points need fixing before it is filed:

1. **The derivation is the ladder shape a recorded decision forbids.** The proposal uses bare CMAC(DHUK, label || prefix). secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs:493-499 records that #36 forbids exactly this, because a transit attacker may learn the deterministic DHUK ladder before the lock; the final OPTIGA PBS mixes a persisted TRNG salt for that reason. Under that threat model, a holder before first boot could compute all 10^4 prefix pairs in software and restore the unit so it still passes the RDP-0 SWD check. That would void the "hours to a day with a button robot" enumeration floor. I did not verify on silicon that DHUK at RDP-1 equals DHUK at RDP-2 after a regression; this rests on the repo's own stated assumption.

2. **The per-boot cap of 3 breaks the feature's own flows.** The wizard already calls enter_pin at least four times: enter_pin_with_confirm is two entries (pin_entry.rs:236-268) and collect_duress_pin calls it again (seed_wizard.rs:251). The idle re-unlock allows up to 12 attempts (main.rs:4448) and fires every 120 s. A legitimate user would routinely reach the "words unavailable, reboot" page. That page then becomes a cover story a trojan can display instead of words.

3. **Cost and priority are optimistic.** The pixel UI is a port of an external PQ-UI reference with a checked deviations file (tools/pq-ui/PORT_DEVIATIONS.toml). A new interstitial on two render paths, a wizard page, a forced-frame test and the salt wiring is M, not S. Every validation prerequisite is blocked (#268, #700, no panel on the bench board), and the feature is advisory with an accepted live-relay residual, so P3 fits better than P2.

4. **The fence is on the wrong signal.** A compile-time rdp2-self-lock gate mislabels RDP-1 bench boards, where DHUK is already per-die (secret_keys.rs:46-50, saes.rs:345-347).

There are no live_defects entries to check.
skeptic.corrections:
1. **Bind the words to the page-127 salt.** Derive as CMAC(DHUK, DOMAIN || journal_salt(32) || prefix_len || prefix) using first_boot::journal_salt_if_all_done (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:83). The salt already exists, is hidden after RDP-2 and persists for device life, so this adds no flash state. It brings the design in line with the rule at secret_keys.rs:493-499 and closes pre-first-boot table precomputation. Phase B runs before the wizard (main.rs:1756-1763), so the salt is available when the user learns the words. If the salt is missing or the ceremony is not ALL_DONE, show the "not device-unique" label and never fall back silently to the unsalted form.

2. **Change the cap semantics.** Count derivations since the last successful gated_unlock and reset on success; exempt set-PIN, confirm-PIN and duress-PIN entry in the wizard. Then a legitimate user never sees "words unavailable", and its appearance is itself an alarm. The cap-per-boot floor adds only about 6.5 h (3,334 boots at ~7 s) on top of roughly 10 h of key presses, so describe it as a modest multiplier, not the main defence.

3. **Domain separation: list every DHUK-axis label.** The proposal omits pqsigner/mlkem-seed-v1 and pqsigner/mlkem-wrap-huk-v1 (secret_keys.rs:314, 324). The KDF framing is CMAC(K, label || 1-byte counter starting at 1) (secure/src/cmac.rs:157-196). A message ending in an ASCII digit (0x30-0x39) cannot equal any existing label || counter, since the longest output needs counters 1-4 and no label ends in the words framing. Give DOMAIN a distinct prefix such as "pqsigner/pin-words-v1\0" and add a const or host test asserting it is not a prefix of any label, and vice versa.

4. **Fence on runtime state, not the compile feature.** Use the RDP level read at runtime plus journal ALL_DONE. A compile-time rdp2-self-lock gate mislabels RDP-1 bench boards.

5. **Fix the threat text.** It cites secure/src/measured_boot.rs:161-170, but measured_boot::run is compiled out under mode-production (main.rs:1750-1751). On a shipping image the only fingerprint is the FSBL's, which is the one #705 reports dark.

6. **Add residuals and doc text.**
   - Any party with access before first boot (factory, transit) can precompute the table if the salt is not mixed in.
   - Words can be viewed with no attempt consumed (long-left back or cancel after the fourth digit), so enumeration never touches page 124, E120 or the SE050 UserID. State this explicitly.
   - "Write these down" creates a paper artifact; if stored near the device, it plus possession yields 4 of 8 digits. Tell the user to memorise the pair or store it apart.
   - The 500 ms long-press figure cited at secure/src/hw/buttons.rs:183 was not re-checked here.

7. **Tracker.** Add #636 (duress-pin implemented but absent from PROD_SHIP_FEATURES) and #280. If duress ships, the user has two prefix pairs unless both PINs share the first four digits; the wizard text must cover that. #772 (closed) is a different feature (seed check words) and should be cited so it is not mistaken for a duplicate.

8. **Pixel UI.** The new screen is a deviation from the PQ-UI reference and must be recorded in tools/pq-ui/PORT_DEVIATIONS.toml. Its transcript and census gates move with it.

9. **Idle re-unlock context.** The interstitial runs inside the PendSV handler. SAES is already used there through gated_unlock's key derivation, so this is not a new reentrancy class, but the review should say so.

10. **Cost S to M, priority P2 to P3.** Kind stays firmware.
